item.title: Darius Acuff Jr. speaks up on big change after losing Ben Simmons to injury
item.description: Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Darius Acuff Jr. speaks up on big change after losing Ben Simmons to injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Sacramento Kings were dealt a major blow over the weekend when it was revealed that Ben Simmons suffered a season-ending Achilles injury. Simmons was attempting an NBA comeback this season after not playing last year, and the Kings had big plans for him, wanting to pair the former No. 1 pick alongside rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr . Losing Ben Simmons to injury hurts the Kings in that his versatile skill set is among the most unique in the NBA. For Darius Acuff and the rest of the team, they’re going to have to find a way to replicate what he brought to the court, as per James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento. “It changes a lot. He was a big part of our team. He can do everything one through five, so it changes a lot,” Acuff said. “I think we’ll figure it out for sure. It hurst to lose him, but I think we’ll figure it out and try to get better at certain things that we know he did.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Simmons had been having a solid preseason and training camp and seemed well on his way to re-establishing himself in the league. Now, the Kings are going to lean a little more on Acuff as the primary ball-handler in Simmons’ absence. With the regular season about to begin, Acuff is coming off a solid preseason debut. The former Arkansas star appeared in four games at a little over 24 minutes per game. He averaged 17.2 points, 1.8 rebounds and 3.8 assists with splits of 42.4 percent shooting from the field, 42.1 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 84.6 percent shooting from the free-throw line. item.title: Padres top trade target is $20 million ace from AL East
item.description: Padres top trade target is $20 million ace from AL East originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Diego Padres could be looking for a new ace next season. Michael King could opt out of the final two years of his contract to become a free agent. Ideally, the Padres would love to retain King and acquire another starter via trade or free agency. Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller believes the offseason could go one of two ways for San Diego's pitching staff. "There's a dream scenario in which Michael King doesn't opt out of the two years left on his contract while both Joe Musgrove and Yu Darvish make triumphant returns in 2027. "There's also a nightmare scenario in which none of those things happen and the Padres are looking at JP Sears, Jhony Brito and Jagger Haynes as regulars in the rotation behind Nick Pivetta and Randy Vásquez," Miller wrote. Miller tabbed Drew Rasmussen as a prime trade target for the Padres. He is the ace of the Tampa Bay Rays and has allowed just three earned runs in 21 postseason innings in 2026. "Maybe they can pry Rasmussen away from Tampa Bay?" Miller added. Just about any club in the Majors would love to have an arm like Rasmussen, who threw a career-high 172 innings this year. MORE : White Sox reportedly have 'no urgency' to sign Munetaka Murakami to an extension He is a lock to finish top 10 in AL Cy Young Award voting for the second straight year. With recent injuries to Musgrove and Darvish, San Diego could use another reliable starter. Rasmussen is one of the best in the business. He could be the difference between losing in the early rounds of the postseason and a run to the World Series. That year, the Wildcats finished 7-6 and lost to Clemson, 38-35, in the Gator Bowl. Now, Stein has Kentucky looking toward bigger goals, including a potential College Football Playoff appearance. His contract also includes several financial incentives tied to the team’s success. Will Stein Contract Incentives According to Stein’s contract, the Kentucky head coach can earn bonuses based on the team’s wins and postseason accomplishments. With Kentucky already at six wins, Stein is one victory away from reaching the seven-win threshold. If the Wildcats defeat Vanderbilt on Saturday at Kroger Field, Stein would receive a $100,000 incentive bonus . For seasons in which Kentucky records 8-to-11 wins, Stein is eligible for a $200,000 bonus for each win in that range, according to the contract language provided. Stein’s contract also rewards conference championship success. If Kentucky reaches the SEC Championship Game, he would receive $100,000. Braylon Mullins didn’t play against Syracuse, and probably will not play in East Lansing. With Mullins figuring to be a major part of the offense this season, UConn will need to find a way to manufacture quality looks without him against a defense that figures to be one of the best in the country. Nik Khamenia stepped up to the challenge against Cuse with 12 points and three 3-pointers, but the Huskies will need more from Ross (two points) and Wofford transfer Nils Machowski (four points) to keep the Sparty defense on their toes.

item.title: Ex-Cowboys star Troy Aikman: 'I love everything about the 49ers organization'
item.description: ESPN commentator Troy Aikman walks the field prior to the game between the Washington Commanders and the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on Oct. 19, 2026, in Santa Clara, Calif. (Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) Troy Aikman spent most of his NFL career right in the heart of the legendary Cowboys-49ers rivalry. But ahead of Monday night's 49ers game against the Commanders, the top analyst for ESPN's "Monday Night Football" broadcasts heaped praise on his former rivals . On ESPN's pregame show, Aikman said he had dinner with former 49ers president Carmen Policy on Sunday night and praised the organization's "consistency and professionalism." He also compared the sustained success the current 49ers are having under Kyle Shanahan to the teams of the 1980s and 1990s. "You look at their style of play ... they play an old-school style of football that the rules of today's game are just simply not supposed to allow you to play - and yet, they do it," Aikman said on "Monday Night Countdown" before the game. "From top to bottom, I just think, over the years, the history that you're talking about, they are so well run from the top to the bottom. I love everything about the 49ers organization." When Aikman was under center, the 49ers and Cowboys faced off in three consecutive NFC title games, with the Cowboys winning two in 1992-93 and the 49ers winning one back in 1994. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Bucks’ Ryan Rollins speaks up on ‘biggest thing’ about backcourt with Tyler Herro appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ryan Rollins is among those expected to take on an even bigger role on the Milwaukee Bucks after the Giannis Antetokounmpo era in Cream City ends. Coming off a breakout season, Rollins is also about to share duties in the backcourt with Milwaukee newcomer Tyler Herro. “I think the biggest thing with us is pushing the pace and creating early offense… me and him have good communication… the more we play we’ll understand each other more,” Rollins said of his partnership with Herro, via Cameron Ezeir of CBS 58 News. Herro arrives on the team as part of a package the Miami Heat sent to Milwaukee in exchange for two-time NBA Most Valuable Player Antetokounmpo and veteran power forward Bobby Portis. “The Greek Freak’s” departure leaves a huge void on the Bucks’ offense and defense, but Rollins and Herro can at least team up to cover for that, at least with their scoring and playmaking. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Herro, a former Sixth-Man of the Year Award winner, is scoring nearly 20.0 points per game in his career. Through 394 games in the league, the former Kentucky Wildcats star has averaged 19.5 points on a 45.0 percent shooting from the floor and 38.2 percent from behind the arc. The 26-year-old Herro is also unselfish with the ball, with a career average of 4.1 assists per outing. Rollins, on the other hand, is looking to build on his strong 2025-26 season in which he averaged 17.3 points, 5.6 assistrs and 4.6 rebounds per outing. item.title: Evan Engram puts ‘encouraging’ spin on Broncos’ offensive brutality
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images. Evan Engram puts ‘encouraging’ spin on Broncos’ offensive brutality appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Denver Broncos tight end Evan Engram remains encouraged by his team’s position despite an underwhelming offensive performance through the first six weeks of the 2026 NFL season. The Broncos enter Week 7 at 4-2, with four wins in their last five games despite lingering concerns about their offensive consistency. Quarterback Bo Nix also boasts an impressive 18-3 record over his last 21 NFL starts. However, Denver’s latest win showcased their ongoing offensive struggles, as the Broncos managed just 168 total yards in a 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday. Still, Engram sees reason for optimism as the team continues to find ways to win without consistently producing their best football. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He acknowledged that the Broncos still have considerable room for improvement while emphasizing the importance of their winning record. The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel shared Engram’s comments Monday on X, formerly Twitter, highlighting the 10th-year NFL veteran’s optimistic outlook despite the team’s offensive struggles. “We’re in a great position after a very tough six weeks.” Engram’s optimism comes after the Broncos’ offense struggled considerably against Seattle at Empower Field at Mile High last Thursday in the opening game of Week 6. Nix completed 17 of 27 passes for 107 yards without a passing touchdown. The Broncos averaged just 2.9 yards per play, according to Seattle’s official game recap. After producing two touchdown drives in the second quarter, Denver managed only two additional first downs through the remainder of regulation. The offense failed to score again until overtime. Cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian intercepted Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold in the extra period, setting up Wil Lutz’s game-winning 53-yard field goal. Head coach Sean Payton addressed those offensive shortcomings Monday, identifying offensive-line execution, rushing efficiency and opportunities for downfield passes as areas requiring improvement. Payton also emphasized that Denver’s offensive struggles extend beyond Nix, placing responsibility on the entire operation, including the coaching staff. The Broncos now prepare to face the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7, seeking their third consecutive victory. Denver’s focus now shifts to improving its offensive efficiency against the Cardinals while building on consecutive victories. item.title: Golden Gophers Weekend Recap
item.description: The Gopher football team may have been on their bye week, but nearly every other Golden Gopher fall sport and several winter ones were in action this past weekend. We saw some epic wins on the ice and on the course as well as on the volleyball court, and a painful loss on the pitch. Below catch a full recap of the weekend action that happened for the Gophers: Women’s Hockey: The Minnesota Golden Gophers headed into their series against #1 Ohio State untested. Minnesota was 4-0 but had defeated Bemidji State who finished last in the WCHA a year ago three times allready. Meanwhile the Buckeyes had taking down #5 Penn State and #2 Wisconsin in a quartet of games prior to their trip to Minneapolis. So the Buckeyes knew what to expect in a tough game from their team, while the Gophers were going to be a mystery. Needless to say, Minnesota is right with the Buckeyes as one of the top teams in the nation. Minnesota took it to Ohio State winning on Friday by a 6-2 score over the #1 team in the country. Freshman Adriani Milani scored her 5th goal of the seas just 14 seconds into the game after intercepting an OSU pass in their defensive end and putting the puck past Buckeye goalie Rowan Houwelling. The Gophers would add two more goals in the opening period from Madison Kaiser and Chloe Primerano to take a 3-0 lead into intermission. Milani made it 4-0 just minutes into the second period and it appeared the Gophers would run away with the game. However, the Buckeyes took advantage of a major penalty to Kaiser for hitting from behind and scored a pair of goals to cut the Gopher lead to 4-2 after two periods. But it was the Gophers night. UConn transfer Ashley Allard scored her first goal in the maroon and gold to make it 5-2, and Kaiser potted her second of the night to round out the 6-2 dominant win for the Gophers. Hannah Clark made 26 saves in the win. Saturday afternoon’s rematch was a ferocious back and forth affair. The Buckeyes came out on fire this time scoring two first period goals and adding another early in the second peirod to take a 3-0 lead. But the Gophes came storming back. Freshman Maddie McCullough scored the first goal for the Gophers 2:30 after the third Buckeye goal to begin the comeback. Freshman Adriani Milani scored her 5th goal of the seas just 14 seconds into the game after intercepting an OSU pass in their defensive end and putting the puck past Buckeye goalie Rowan Houwelling. The Gophers would add two more goals in the opening period from Madison Kaiser and Chloe Primerano to take a 3-0 lead into intermission. Milani made it 4-0 just minutes into the second period and it appeared the Gophers would run away with the game. However, the Buckeyes took advantage of a major penalty to Kaiser for hitting from behind and scored a pair of goals to cut the Gopher lead to 4-2 after two periods. But it was the Gophers night. UConn transfer Ashley Allard scored her first goal in the maroon and gold to make it 5-2, and Kaiser potted her second of the night to round out the 6-2 dominant win for the Gophers. Freshman Maddie McCullough scored the first goal for the Gophers 2:30 after the third Buckeye goal to begin the comeback. Sophomore Avery Hovland scored her first goal of the season next to cut the lead to 3-2. item.title: 49ers’ Brock Purdy gets ‘stud’ endorsement from John Lynch before MNF
item.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images 49ers’ Brock Purdy gets ‘stud’ endorsement from John Lynch before MNF appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Kyle Shanahan ’s San Francisco 49ers faced a tough test on Monday Night Football in Week 6, welcoming the Washington Commanders to Levi’s Stadium amid a positive Mike Evans injury update . Another well known Brock Purdy weapon was ruled out as Purdy got an endorsement from general manager John Lynch before the game. Lynch’s pride for his star quarterback was palpable as he explained it to Pat McAfee before the big game. “He’s a stud, he has been from the time he got here. I tell people all the time, don’t count your reps, make your reps count…He’s not being safe, he’s ripping (the ball) in tight windows, ever since then we knew we had a player. He’s done nothing but get better this entire time.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McAfee shared with Lynch that Purdy is five pass attempts from becoming the NFL’s all-time leader for best passer rating. As Purdy continues to evolve, the record books, and a potential Super Bowl, are both becoming clear goals as the 49ers star makes the most out of the opportunities he’s been given with one of the league’s top franchises. Purdy received a co-MVP take from Colin Cowherd earlier this week , and fans around the NFL are starting to take notice. The 49ers are 5-0 with a revolving door of a supporting cast, and Purdy has made the most of it each week in the Bay Area. A win over the Commanders would draw the 49ers closer to home field advantage in the playoffs, something that could make a big difference considering how well Purdy and his teammates play at home. Purdy doesn’t get the same type of hype of guys like Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, but he has the talent, and the work ethic, to get the most out of his considerable skills in a way that few other quarterbacks are capable of doing. item.title: Boston Celtics alum Doc Rivers exhorts us to vote, pointing to civil rights struggles
item.description: Recently retired Boston Celtics head coach Doc Rivers has never been shy in front of a microphone. Even when the topic is not sports but politics, the 2008 champion will say his piece when he feels the issue rises to the appropriate level of concern. And he has faced backlash for that frankness, even if it is also supported by others. And Rivers felt the need to wade into the status quo when it comes to US politics this week during a recent interview with MS Now as Election Day draws closer. "My mom stood in the rain, and my dad stood in the rain to vote," said Rivers. "And they voted because… the candidate wasn't the perfect candidate, probably, in their minds. I don't know why they were voting whichever way they voted. But one reason they voted is because they actually could. Because half their lifetime, they couldn't. And so I used to remember my mom would get dressed up to go vote. Like it was like her Sunday outfit, to go vote." "And when you think about that, and (that) we didn't have to do any of that. And so voting has been made ... it's becoming hard again," said the Celtics coaching alum. "But at one point, it was made so easy, we didn't do it (...)," said Rivers. "We took it for granted, and we are learning now where it can be taken away from you, and you have to keep working on it. I swear there's so many similarities to sports. It's unbelievable." "If you stop working in sports, if you take anything for granted in sports, if you take (it for granted), you're just going to continue to win, you'll start losing. You've got to keep doing the work. And honestly ... we stopped doing all the work, and it's hurt all of us." Listen to "A look at the Pritchard extension, Boston Celtics preseason play, and more" on Spreaker. item.title: Giants HC John Harbaugh Puts Cam Skattebo on Notice: ‘Do Something’
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 04: Cam Skattebo #44 of the New York Giants looks on during an injury timeout in the fourth quarter against the Arizona Cardinals at MetLife Stadium on October 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) Getty The New York Giants’ Week 6 game against the New Orleans Saints proved to be more eventful than perhaps originally anticipated. Hours before the game, reports surfaced that veteran running back Najee Harris would get the start over second-year player Cam Skattebo, as Skattebo was set to have his role reduced on the team. That played out as three different Giants running backs ran the ball against the Saints. Meanwhile, Skattebo was only on the field for six snaps and did not register a carry. Apparently, this did not please any of the team’s running backs. After the game Najee Harris expressed frustration with his role, as he stated that he felt he should have received more than four carries after being told he was starting. Despite head coach John Harbaugh refusing to state that Skattebo was benched, the running back felt he was being punishe d after his costly fumble against the Washington Commanders Now, head coach John Harbaugh has issued a statement on the team’s running back situation. Giants Head Coach John Harbaugh Puts Cam Skattebo on Notice View this post on Instagram ESPN’s Jordan Raanan posted on X: “John Harbaugh says he knows and understands how Najee Harris and the RBs feel about the 4-man rotation. They all want t be the No. 1 guy. But Harbaugh says he also knows that carries are “earned” and tells them “do something” in their opportunities and more will come.” John Harbaugh says he knows and understands how Najee Harris and the RBs feel about the 4-man rotation. They all want t be the No. 1 guy. But Harbaugh says he also knows that carries are "earned" and tells them "do something" in their opportunities and more will come. — Jordan Raanan (@JordanRaanan) October 19, 2026 Harbaugh’s comments echo a similar thing to what he said directly after the team’s loss against the New Orleans Saints. Harbaugh told reporters on Sunday, “You can say, well, I don’t like that. I don’t like you divvying up the snaps between four backs. And I can tell you, I don’t like it either. item.title: Buffalo Bills Release 3-Year Veteran CB After Tre’Davious White Signing
item.description: Bills release A.J. Woods. Getty Bills bring back Tre'Davious White. Getty The Buffalo Bills made some changes to their practice roster during their bye week. Buffalo is coming off a 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders to enter the bye week with a record of 5-1. The Bills’ defense, however, has been an issue, and Buffalo has been urged to make some moves to help bolster it, especially the secondary. Buffalo Bills Make CB Moves Getty Bills bring back Tre’Davious White. The Bills made a move on their practice squad, as the team released three-year veteran cornerback A.J. Woods, the team announced on Monday . Woods signed with the Bills’ practice squad on October 6 after he was part of the Atlanta Falcons ‘ final roster cuts in August. The 25-year-old cornerback went undrafted in the 2024 NFL Draft out of Pitt and signed with the Washington Commanders . He was waived in August and signed with the Philadelphia Eagles ‘ practice squad. Woods was on the Eagles’ practice squad for the entire year and is considered a Super Bowl champion as Philadelphia won it all that year. He signed a reserve/future contract in February but was released in August. Woods then spent time with the Denver Broncos and Falcons in 2025. Although Woods has been in the NFL for three years, he’s never played in a game and instead has just spent time on practice squads and offseason rosters. At Pitt, Woods was an impact cornerback. In his senior year, he recorded 30 tackles, 2 sacks, and 1 interception . In his five-year college career, he recorded 105 tackles, 2 sacks, and 4 interceptions. Buffalo Brings Back White The Bills released Woods because the team signed White to their practice squad. This will be White’s third stint in Buffalo after being drafted in 2017 and playing until 2023. He returned to Buffalo last season and had a major role in the defense. White started in 16 games, totaling 10 passes defensed, one interception, and 40 tackles. In his lone year away from the Bills in 2024, he spent time with the Baltimore Ravens and Los Angeles Rams . White is expected to use time on the practice squad to get accustomed to Jim Leonhard’s defense before signing to the active roster, according to Adam Schefter. “CB Tre’Davious White is signing with the Bills’ practice squad, where he will acclimate before joining their active roster. White turned down several opportunities to return to Buffalo. White started 16 regular-season games and two playoff games last season. His agents, Kevin Conner and Robert Brown of unisportsmgmt , confirmed the signing,” Schefter wrote on X . The Bills are on their bye week and will host the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8. So, White will have time to get accustomed to the defense and help bolster the secondary. item.title: Jake Paul Asks UFC to Cut Jon Jones for Francis Ngannou Fight
item.description: Jon Jones Jake Paul Francis Ngannou Getty MVP promoter Jake Paul asked the UFC to cut legend Jon Jones so he can fight Francis Ngannou in Paul’s promotion. Zuffa Boxing, which is run by UFC president Dana White, released boxer Shakur Stevenson today, despite the company typically not releasing fighters That led Paul to take to social media and ask the UFC to cut Jones, so he can go to MVP and fight Ngannou, whom White despises and who has said will never fight again in the UFC. Jake Paul Asks UFC to Release Jon Jones Taking to his social media, Paul formally requested that the UFC release Jones so he can fight Ngannou in MVP, though he did not specify if that would be for a boxing match or MMA fight. “Can Jon Jones request a release like Shakur Stevenson so we can go ahead and do this Francis Ngannou vs Jon Jones fight? They already said they are never working with Francis. So let Jon fly and we can give the fans what they want. Please and thank you. @JonnyBones @francis_ngannou,” Paul wrote on his X . Can Jon Jones request a release like Shakur Stevenson so we can go ahead and do this Francis Ngannou vs Jon Jones fight? They already said they are never working with Francis. So let Jon fly and we can give the fans what they want. Please and thank you. @JonnyBones … — Jake Paul (@jakepaul) October 19, 2026 Dana White Unlikely to Release Jon Jones Though Jones may want to be released from the UFC, especially knowing he has a fight offer to take on Ngannou in MVP floating around, it’s highly unlikely that White lets Jones go and fight for a rival combat sports promotion. White typically does not let fighters go when they ask for their release, especially when it comes to big-name stars like Jones or Sean Strickland , the UFC middleweight champion who is in a similar position at the moment. Most likely, White will just ignore what Paul said about releasing Jones, as the chances of the UFC doing that are slim to none anyways. For Jones, he would surely love to get his walking papers so he can go out there and get a big-money fight with Ngannou, a matchup that never materialized in the UFC for whatever reason. But again, the odds of him getting a clean contract release from the UFC are pretty much as close to zero as possible. item.title: Canucks Head Coach Manny Malhotra Remains Focused On The Future When It Comes To Defenceman Zeev Buium
item.description: The Vancouver Canucks clearly have big hopes for defenceman Zeev Buium. The 20-year-old signed an eight-year extension this off-season that carries an AAV of $9.38 million while also being named to the leadership group. Overall, the early production from Buium has been surprising, as he sits with just one assist through his first 10 games. Buium's performances so far this season have become a major talking point in the market. Over the past few games, part of that discussion has focused on Manny Malhotra's decision to change his d-pairing and move the former 12th overall pick to the third pair. After practice on Monday, the Canucks head coach was about what he has seen from Buium in what can be considered a sheltered role. "Well, you call it a shelter role; he's a 20-year-old defenseman learning the league," said Malhotra. "So, for all the words that I've heard thrown out there, demotion or shelter role, he's still learning his game. He's learning the league. So, not something that we didn't expect to occur for a 20-year-old defenseman. This is just a part of the growing process for him." There are few 20-year-olds in the league with more pressure placed upon them than Buium. As mentioned, he signed the massive deal that kicks in next year, but he is also seen as a current and future face of the franchise. When asked whether the extra pressure has impacted Buium, Malhotra stressed that the focus remains on his long-term success. "Potentially, that's a reason. But from our standpoint, we've made it very clear to him that we are focused on the long game. You know, the day-to-day of what pairing you're on and how many minutes you're getting, we don't want to be short-sighted in that regard and put pressure there. He understands that we're focused on his overall growth for year 2, 3, 4, and 5, kind of thing." How Buium develops is a key factor in the success of this rebuild. If developed correctly, he has the potential to become a top-pair defender and a leader once this team becomes a playoff contender. Ultimately, it is clear that Malhotra and the organization have a plan to help Buium develop into a star at the NHL level. item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Have any footballers ended their career with more own goals than goals? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the earliest trophyless seasons, scoring off one’s backside (part II) and the origins of ‘shithousery’ Mail us with all of your questions and answers “How many professional players have ended their senior careers with more own goals than goals for their own team?” wonders Peter Clark. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
